title: River valleys, food surplus and the first cities
observableEvidence: Selects the physical feature of the Tigris, Euphrates and Nile river valleys that supported permanent farming settlements in a dry climate: river floods left fertile silt and river water could reach the crops.

Selects, from a short original account of early Mesopotamian farming, the correct cause and the correct effect of a food surplus: irrigation canals helped produce the surplus, and the surplus let some people do work other than farming.
